chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to the mosque while they are in prayer, and the Imam has already preceded him by one rak'ah or more. So the Imam stands up (for a brief rest or action), takes his hand, and he is the closest of the people to him, so he appoints him as Imam. He said: 'He completes the prayer with the people, then sits until they finish the Tashahhud. He signals with his hand to them from the right and from the left, and what he signaled with his hand to them was the Taslim (greeting of peace) and the conclusion of their prayer. And he completes for himself whatever was missed or remained upon him.'
And it has been narrated that he appoints another man, with whom he performs the Taslim, and he completes for himself whatever remained. And this is the more precautionary (preferred) view.
ai.seo_question: How does a latecomer complete their prayer if they join after the Imam has already prayed one or more rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific jurisprudence for a latecomer (*Ma'mum*) joining the congregational prayer (*Salat al-Jama'ah*) after the Imam has already completed one or more rak'ahs. It outlines two primary methods: either the latecomer assumes the role of Imam to lead the remaining prayer and conclude with Taslim, or he remains a follower and completes his own prayer independently. The text notes that appointing another person to lead the Taslim for the group is considered the more cautious (*ahwat*) opinion, reflecting the nuanced scholarly debate in Shia fiqh regarding the continuity of congregational unity.
